content: Mittelschmerz refers to one-sided lower abdominal pain experienced by women around the time of ovulation, when an egg is released from the ovaries. Symptoms of Mittelschmerz: The pain may alternate sides each month or remain on the same side for several consecutive months. It is characterized by lower abdominal pain that is: One-sided. Typically lasting from a few minutes to a few hours, but in some cases, it can persist for 24 to 48 hours. Usually sharp, cramping, and distinctive in nature. Rarely severe. May switch sides from one month to the next or between episodes. Occurs midway through the menstrual cycle. Causes of Mittelschmerz: Approximately 1 in 5 women experience Mittelschmerz, which is pain associated with ovulation. The pain can occur just before, during, or after ovulation. Possible explanations for the pain include: Just before ovulation: The growth of the follicle may stretch the surface of the ovary, causing discomfort. During ovulation: Fluid or blood released from the ruptured egg follicle may irritate the abdominal lining, leading to pain. When to Seek Medical Care: Contact your healthcare provider if ovulation pain changes in nature, lasts longer than usual, or is accompanied by vaginal bleeding. Diagnosis: A pelvic examination typically reveals no abnormalities. Additional tests, such as an abdominal ultrasound or transvaginal pelvic ultrasound, may be performed to rule out other causes of ovarian or pelvic pain if the discomfort persists. Treatment Options: In most cases, no treatment is necessary. Pain relievers (analgesics) may be used for prolonged or intense pain. Medical Care for Mittelschmerz: Directions to hospitals or clinics treating Mittelschmerz can be sought if needed. Prognosis: While Mittelschmerz can be painful, it is not harmful and is not indicative of any underlying disease. Women who experience this pain may find it helpful for family planning, as it occurs around ovulation. A woman is most likely to conceive just before, during, or immediately after ovulation. Possible Complications: There are usually no complications associated with Mittelschmerz. Prevention: Birth control pills can be used to prevent ovulation and reduce ovulation-related pain.
